newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen, foreign firms discuss $5 bln LNG project.
newsitem.headline: Yemen, foreign firms discuss $5 bln LNG project.

text.p: Officials from Yemen and France's Total SA, U.S. Exxon Corp, Hunt Oil and South Korea's Yukong are holding talks in Sanaa on firming equity shares in a consortium to develop a $5 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in the Arab state.
"The negotiations are proceeding in a good way to reach a final agreement that might be signed within the next few days," an Oil Ministry official told Reuters on Thursday.
He did not give other details.
Yemeni officials and the foreign firms had held talks in Paris in October last year.

In January last year, Exxon, Hunt and Yukong signed a memorandum of participation in the planned LNG project which will be operated by Total. Under this agreement Hunt-Exxon would jointly hold 38 percent of the project's shares, Total 36 percent and the Yemeni government 26 percent.
The proposed LNG plant at Balhaf on the Arabian Sea aims to export an annual five million tonnes of gas to Asian and European markets from the year 2001.
